While the confidence intervals are designed to encompass 90% of expected outcomes, certain extreme or unforeseen events, often referred to as "tail risks," could push the actual results outside these predicted ranges. These low-probability, high-impact events are inherently difficult to quantify precisely within standard probabilistic models, meaning they always pose a risk of defying even broad forecast ranges.
